item.summary: fix: /models stops working after an unrelated config edit and never recovers (#128608) * fix: /models stops working after an unrelated config edit and never recovers A config transaction whose reload plan is empty publishes the new runtime config but never advances the prepared model owner's config stamp. Owners are stamped with a hash of the whole config, so a key with no bearing on models leaves every strict-policy catalog read rejected for the life of the gateway process. Advance the model-neutral config stamp in place on no-op publications instead of rebuilding the prepared generation, which the planner has already determined is unnecessary. Existing leases keep their immutable snapshot, auth bindings carry onto the restamped snapshot, pending builds restamp at commit, and read-only owners are untouched. Deferred startup publication now resolves its config inside the serialized refresh so a no-op commit landing mid-startup cannot publish an already-stale stamp.
